description: Multiply the total gross monthly earned income by 20 percent and subtract that amount from the total gross income.

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module claimed to encode 7 CFR 273.10(e) net-income and benefit-level mechanics but jumped straight from gross income to the excess-shelter step, omitting the (e)(1)(i)(A) income exclusions and the entire (B)-(G) deduction sequence (20 percent earned-income deduction, standard deduction, medical expenses over $35, dependent care, child support, homeless shelter deduction capped at $143) as well as the (e)(2)(ii)(A) allotment formula and the (e)(2)(ii)(C) minimum benefit for one- and two-person households.
triage.triage_notes: Largest rewrite in the commit (98 -> 403 lines). Pre-fix rules were only snap_gross_monthly_income (= countable earned + countable unearned, with no '- exclusions'), snap_monthly_household_income, snap_excess_shelter_income_offset_rate, snap_half_adjusted_income, snap_uncapped_excess_shelter_deduction, snap_excess_shelter_deduction, snap_initial_month_minimum_issuance_threshold, snap_initial_month_allotment_after_minimum_issuance; the module produced no net monthly income and no allotment at all. Post-fix also adds a carve-out that excess shelter cost is 0 when the homeless shelter deduction is taken, and the (e)(2)(ii)(A) rounding option branch. Effective dates unchanged at 2025-10-01 throughout. triage.verifier_justification: The first reader's stated reading is refuted on the facts: the pre-fix module did not "jump straight from gross income to the excess-shelter step" — it imported `us:statutes/7/2014/e/6/A` and fed the 50 percent step with `snap_net_income_pre_shelter`, which that statutory module computed as gross income minus the standard, earned-income, dependent-care, child-support and medical deductions, with the 20 percent rate encoded in `statutes/7/2014/e/2.yaml` and the allotment/30 percent/8 percent minimum benefit already encoded in `statutes/7/2017/a.yaml`. So the quoted 20 percent excerpt witnesses a deduction that was already encoded and consumed, and most of this diff re-homes existing statutory coverage into the regulation module rather than correcting wrong meaning. A narrower unrepresented_clause basis does survive — the (e)(1)(i)(G) homeless shelter deduction and the (e)(1)(i)(H) "unless a deduction has been subtracted in accordance with (G)" carve-out existed nowhere in the repo at the parent commit — but the commit subject is generic ("Regenerate validated US RuleSpec encodings", empty body) and the PR body is about 26 USC 63(c) and never mentions 7 CFR 273.10, so nothing settles whether that omission was the point of the change.

That module defines `snap_net_income_pre_shelter = max(0, snap_monthly_household_income - snap_standard_deduction - snap_earned_income_deduction - dependent_care_deduction - child_support_deduction - medical_deduction)`, and imports `statutes/7/2014/e/2.yaml`, which holds `snap_earned_income_deduction_rate = 0.20`. The pre-fix `snap_monthly_household_income` rule that the reader read as a dead alias is in fact the input that module consumes (`statutes/7/2014/e/6/A.yaml:26`), so the pre-fix chain was a deliberate delegation, not an omission.
- (e)(2)(ii)(A) and (C) were likewise already encoded at the parent in `statutes/7/2017/a.yaml`: 30 percent contribution rate, `floor(max(0, snap_maximum_allotment - snap_household_food_contribution))`, and `floor((snap_one_person_thrifty_food_plan_cost * 0.08) + 0.5)` for `household_size <= 2`. Their appearance in 273.10 is duplicated regulatory coverage.
- No number was corrected: 0.50 and 10 survive unchanged; 0.20, 35, 143, 0.30, 0.08 and 2 are newly introduced, so amount_mismatch does not fit better. Effective dates all stay '2025-10-01', entity/period stay Household/Month, and no boolean was inverted, so the other kinds are out.
- What was genuinely absent repo-wide: `git grep -l homeless` over statutes/7 at the parent returns nothing, and the only regulations hit is `regulations/7-cfr/273/24.yaml`, whose "homeless" reference is an ABAWD exemption (`or member_is_homeless`), not the shelter deduction. The $35 medical threshold was also only an unencoded input hook (`medical_deduction` was a bare input). The added branch `if snap_homeless_shelter_deduction_for_net_income > 0: 0` is well grounded in (e)(1)(i)(H) ("Total the allowable shelter expenses ... unless a deduction has been subtracted in accordance with paragraph (e)(1)(i)(G)").
- Source text verified through the pinned release us-sc-snap-2026-07-15 (expression date 2026-07-09) via resolve_provision.py for us/regulation/7/273/10; every proof-atom excerpt added by the fix is verbatim in that text.
